Reviewer fix: Guangxi (Cangwu, Yulin) is out. The page names the family's posts as Jiaozhi (Shi Xie), Hepu (Shi Yi), Jiuzhen (Shi Wei) and Nanhai (Shi Wu); Cangwu's Administrator was Wu Ju, appointed by Liu Biao, whom Bu Zhi killed in 210. Hepu is drawn as a Beihai 100 km circle, Nanhai as Guangdong, Jiaozhi/Jiuzhen/Rinan as the Han 197 shape within Vietnam; the page does not define the seven commanderies, so this is five of them.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 210-227: the same land under Wu: Shi Xie 'led his followers to submit to Bu Zhi's governorship' (footnote 14: Jian'an 15 = 210, Sun Quan sent Bu Zhi as Inspector of Jiao; Shi Xie led his brothers to accept his orders; Bu Zhi killed Wu Ju of Cangwu), General of the Left 210-220 (infobox); he 'died of illness in 226 ... after ruling Jiaozhi for a total of 40 years'; his son Shi Hui held it until 227. Sun Quan then split it: Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen and Rinan stayed in Jiao; Cangwu, Nanhai, Yulin and Hepu formed Guang. Cangwu and Yulin were never the family's on the page, so they are not drawn (reviewer fix).

ledger.note: 207, bridged: the commanderies of the Shi family. A Han decree put him 'in charge of the seven commanderies in Jiao Province' (decree text, footnote 12: 董督七郡, 領交阯太守如故); his brothers were administrators of Hepu, Jiuzhen and Nanhai (no appointment dates). The decree is undated: it follows Zhu Fu's killing (200) and Zhang Jin's governorship (203, footnote 10) and precedes the 207 promotion to General Who Stabilises Distant Lands, which the page calls a further promotion, so 207 is the ceiling date (confidence 1). PAGE SILENT. The region is the five commanderies the page names for the family; Cangwu (Wu Ju, Liu Biao's man) and Yulin are not drawn.

210: Shi Xie submits to Sun Quan's governor. Footnote 14 (Sanguozhi): 「建安十五年,孫權遣步隲為交州刺史。隲到,燮率兄弟奉承節度。而吳巨懷異心,隲斬之。」 (gloss: in Jian'an 15 = 210 Sun Quan sent Bu Zhi as Inspector of Jiao Province, Shi Xie led his brothers to accept his orders, and Bu Zhi killed Wu Ju of Cangwu); the main text: he 'led his followers to submit to Bu Zhi's governorship'; General of the Left (infobox 210-220). The ruling family keeps the land under a new overlord, so this is a vassal tie (retyped from rename in the repair pass); in 210 Cao Cao had conferred the nine bestowments on him to win him against Sun Quan. eastern-wu (ea-03) is not yet written.

ledger.note: 227: the tie ends. After Shi Xie's death in 226 'in 227 he [Shi Hui] refused to hand over Jiaozhi and blocked Dai Liang and Chen Shi'; Lü Dai then 'recaptured the commandery, executed Shi Hui and his brothers' (see the contest and the loss).

227: Shi Hui resists Wu. After his father's death in 226 'in 227 he refused to hand over Jiaozhi and blocked Dai Liang and Chen Shi'; Sun Quan had split Jiao from Guang 'around the time' of Shi Xie's death.
227: Lü Dai ends it. He 'recaptured the commandery, executed Shi Hui and his brothers, and sent their heads to Sun Quan at Wuchang'.

notes:
Shi Xie, the Jiaozhi of the Shi family, 187-227. 2 pages opened (Shi Xie, Eastern Wu); no Cliopatria row. Cliopatria's Han rows (to 237; ea-02-c marks the 224-237 row wrong) and its Eastern Wu shape from 238 (reaching 16.9 N) cover the land; Eastern Wu's 207-237 shape (609,286 km2, south to 22.5 N) does not reach Vietnam, so Vietnam 224-237 is only in the Han row that ea-02-c marked wrong.
Unsettled: (1) the decree giving him the seven commanderies is undated (c. 207 is his promotion: confidence 1); (2) the page does not define the seven commanderies beyond naming Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan, Hepu, Nanhai, Cangwu (Yulin only in the later split); (3) the capital is not on the Shi Xie page; (4) the page gives no 210 month for the submission to Bu Zhi; (5) the Book of Liang names a different administrator in 226 (Wu Miao): footnote conflict; (6) the Trung sisters (43-50, se-01) and the Lin-yi/Champa foundation (192, se-01) are neighbours; neither is reconciled here.
Counterparts: han-dynasty, eastern-wu exist.
Repair pass (ea-02-x-fixed): (1) K0 split: Jiaozhi alone 187-206, the family's commanderies from 207 (the decree is undated: after 200 and Zhang Jin's 203 governorship, before the 207 promotion described as 'further'; 207 is the ceiling). (2) Guangxi (Cangwu, Yulin) removed: the page gives the family Jiaozhi, Hepu, Jiuzhen and Nanhai; Hepu is a Beihai 100 km circle, Nanhai stands as Guangdong; Cangwu's Administrator Wu Ju (Liu Biao's man) was killed by Bu Zhi in 210. (3) The 210 'rename' is now vassal_start with eastern-wu and the 227 vassal_end is added; eastern-wu is ea-03's and not yet written. (4) The Shi Yi page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shi_Yi_(Han_dynasty)) returned URL_NOT_FOUND, so the brothers' appointment dates remain unknown. The seven commanderies are still not listed on the Shi Xie page.
